title: CHAPTER FIFTEEN. On eternal death
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): These things concerning eternal life: there follows eternal death, ye which stands as ye separation belonging toward ye impious out from God plus all ye saints because belonging toward impenitence plus unbelief, plus so their own malice, in ye which together with ye Devil they will endure without end ye wrath belonging toward God, ye bite belonging toward conscience, plus thence ignominy belonging toward every kind plus anxiety together with unspeakable torment. || On eternal death. Caput ye fifteenth.
pass_b_english: These things concerning eternal life: there follows eternal death, which is the separation of the impious from God and all the saints because of impenitence and unbelief, and so their own malice, in which with the Devil they will endure without end the wrath of God, the bite of conscience, and thence ignominy of every kind and anxiety with unspeakable torment.
source_text: CAPUT DECIMUMQUINTUM. De aeterna morte. Haec de vita aeterna: sequitur mors aeterna, quae est impiorum separatio a Deo & omnibus sanctis propter impoenitentiam & incredulitatem, adeoque malitiam suam, in qua cum Diabolo iram Dei conscientia morsus, indeque omnis generis ignominiam & anxietatem cum ineffabili cruciatu sine fine perpetientur.
